summary: Sorust dual native artifacts and reusable kernels

delivery.outcome: Build compiled Python extensions and reusable atomic Rust cdylibs in platform wheels with checksums, versioned C ABI, parity tests and adoption guidance for nl-* consumers. Continue through GitHub PR and independent protected merge under the user publication request of 2026-11-09; initial-ref publication requires its separate protected grant.
nonGoals: Migrate existing consumer repositories, publish to package registries, forge initial-ref grants, disable hooks or perform author approval/merge.
Claim automatic speedup for arbitrary Python, stable Rust ABI or cross-platform validation from one host.

architecture.decision: Use Cython for explicitly selected Python modules and Cargo cdylib plus rlib for independent Rust kernels. A PEP517 backend packages both artifacts with an integrity manifest. A versioned C ABI permits cross-language sharing; explicit native selection fails on missing or corrupt binaries.
architecture.rollback: Remove this isolated consumer dependency or revert through protected review; preserve existing consumer code.

validation.evidence: Wheel and sdist rebuild each contain an importable compiled Python module and a Rust shared library with matching manifest hashes.
Byte corpus parity, ABI null/empty checks, integrity rejection, independent wheel installation and Rust/C consumer reuse.
Bounded local governance and canonical documentation checks; no claim of remote approval.
